<!--
WHAT THIS IS. `figure_4_supplement_recursive_ladder.Rmd` with one knob changed, `FIG4_ANCHOR <-
"sim"`, exactly as `figure_4_sim.Rmd` is `figure_4.Rmd` with that knob. Same roster (R, MR, VR,
IR), same 16 columns, same `per_row`, same scale, same lines. The distortion half is read from
`battery_sim_G` instead of `battery_pool_G`; the bias half does not move, because it was always
read at theta_sim and a pool-anchored bias is zero by construction.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE HERE THAN IN THE BODY. The body figure's members split cleanly: IR, INR and
LSE showed no anchor effect at all (median |log(GIDM_sim/GIDM_pool)| of 0.003 or less over the
whole plane), R showed a large one, NR a moderate one, and the size tracked the misspecification
bias. This supplement's roster is the OPPOSITE selection: R is the member with the largest anchor
effect measured so far, and MR and VR carry biases of the same order (+0.18 and +0.13 in log10
N_ch at noise 0.1, against R's +0.14 and IR's +0.0003). So three of the four columns here are
members whose two anchors are known or expected to disagree, and the ladder claim is stated in
pool-anchored numbers.

THE CLAIM UNDER TEST. The pool-anchored file says the rungs do not interpolate: R to IR is a
factor 1.45 in the k_off distortion and MR sits ABOVE R (1.94 against 1.46 at N_ch 1e4), with VR
recovering part of it. If that ordering is an artefact of reading each member at its own displaced
theta_pool, it changes; if it survives at a common anchor it is a property of the closures. Either
answer is worth having, and only one of them is currently in the file.

The comparison chunk at the bottom prints both anchors side by side for the four rungs, so the
header table of the pool file can be read against this one line for line.

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE, and it is worth saying because it is the honest half of the argument. The
BIAS half is identical in the two files, so everything the pool file says about the first moment
stands untouched: MR's +0.195 against R's +0.139 against IR's +0.0003 is a theta_sim measurement
already. If the second-moment ordering turns out to be anchor-dependent and the first-moment one
is not, the ladder claim survives in the moment where it is cleanest.

COVERAGE is the same ragged staircase as the pool file: R and IR to noise 1e7 at N_ch 1e4, MR at
three levels and VR at two, rows pinned to the union so the unswept part shows as grey. VR falls
under MIN_CONTOUR_LEVELS and draws as tiles. Nothing here changes that; it reverts as the runs
land.

CAVEAT CARRIED FROM THE BODY WORK. `Dconf` is the CI EDGE toward 1, not the point estimate, so a
1.000 in any of these tables means "the 95 per cent interval brackets 1" and not "the distortion
is one". The comparison chunk prints the point estimate `m` alongside for that reason.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

```{r common, include=FALSE}
# Identical to the pool file, plus the anchor.
FIG4_ALGOS     <- c("macro_R", "macro_MR", "macro_VR", "macro_IR")
FIG4_ALGO_LAB  <- c(macro_R = "R", macro_MR = "MR", macro_VR = "VR", macro_IR = "IR")
FIG4_DATA_DIRS <- c("../data/1c2ae6f", "../data/87889e6", "../data/0ffbda7", "../data/1f7138b")
FIG4_ANCHOR    <- "sim"
source("figure_4_common.R")
source("figure_4_layout.R")
```

```{r sides}
# `bias` is unchanged (always sim-anchored); `stat` is now the sim-anchored distortion.
SIDES <- list(
  list(lab = "distortion-induced bias", letter = "A",
       data = bias,                                  zf = function(x) x$Bconf),
  list(lab = "information distortion at the truth",  letter = "B",
       data = dplyr::filter(stat, comp == "total"),  zf = function(x) log10(x$Dconf)))
```

```{r render, fig.width = 7.4, fig.height = 6.63}
# 16 columns, same layout as the pool file, so the same measured per_row.
fig4_render(SIDES, per_row = 0.204,
            out = "Figure_4_supplement_recursive_ladder_sim.pdf")
```

```{r compare, echo=FALSE}
# The two anchors line by line, in the shape of the pool file's header table: medians over the
# seven intervals at noise 0.1. Dconf is what the map paints (CI edge toward 1); m is the point
# estimate, which is what an ordering claim has to be made on.
cmp <- .fig4_all$stat %>%
  dplyr::filter(algo %in% ALGOS, comp == "total", noise == "0.1",
                param %in% c("off", "Num_ch_mean")) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(param, algo, Num_ch, anchor) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(Dconf = median(Dconf), m = median(m), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = anchor, values_from = c(Dconf, m)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(algo = factor(ALGO_LAB[algo], levels = ALGO_LAB[ALGOS])) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(param, algo, Num_ch)
cat("\n=== the recursive ladder at both anchors, noise 0.1, median over the 7 intervals ===\n")
cat("Dconf = CI edge toward 1 (what the map paints); m = the point estimate\n\n")
print(as.data.frame(cmp), digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)

# Does the ORDERING of the four rungs survive the anchor change? Reported per parameter and N_ch,
# on the point estimate, because that is what the ladder claim is about.
ord <- cmp %>% dplyr::group_by(param, Num_ch) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(pool = paste(algo[order(m_pool)], collapse = " < "),
                   sim  = paste(algo[order(m_sim)],  collapse = " < "),
                   same = identical(order(m_pool), order(m_sim)), .groups = "drop")
cat("\n=== ordering of the rungs, cheapest distortion first ===\n\n")
print(as.data.frame(ord), row.names = FALSE)
```
